evals.prompt: Group the open P1 issues into sets I can each work on in a single PR.
evals.expected_output: Cohesive groups, each with a platform tag (shared/android/ios/both), the files it touches, a merge order, and a parallelism verdict. Shared-module fixes are tagged [shared] and ordered before platform-specific work. iOS-only parity divergences (Android already guards) are tagged [ios].
expectations: Every group carries a platform tag of shared, android, ios, or both
Every group names the files it touches, resolved to their real path (shared/src/commonMain, app/src/main, or iosApp/)
A fix that lives in shared/src/commonMain is identified as fixing both platforms in one edit and ordered shared-before-platform
An explicit merge order is given, marking which groups are parallel (disjoint files)
The long pole is named, with a statement of whether the rest ships without it

evals.prompt: Which of these can I do in one PR: 607, 608? (skill argument: 607,608)
evals.expected_output: One group containing both, tagged [ios], justified as the same parity-divergence root cause — iOS restore/reset destroys data that Android already guards — even though they sit in different files (LearnRepository.swift and PracticeTimerRepository.swift).
expectations: #607 and #608 are placed in a single group
The justification is the shared root cause: an iOS restore/reset path overwrites or deletes data that Android's equivalent path preserves
The group is tagged as iOS-only (both fixes are in iosApp/ Swift files; Android is already correct)
Both files are named: iosApp/UkuleleCompanion/Repositories/LearnRepository.swift and .../PracticeTimerRepository.swift

evals.prompt: Is issue 609 one PR on its own or can it be batched with the iOS restore bugs 607 and 608? (skill argument: 607,608,609)
evals.expected_output: Two groups: #609 alone tagged [shared] because it is a fix in shared/src/commonMain PracticeRoutineGenerator.kt that fixes both platforms at once, and #607+#608 as a separate [ios] parity group. #609 is not merged with the iOS bugs — different surface, different root cause.
expectations: #609 is placed in its own group, separate from #607/#608
#609 is identified as a shared-module fix (shared/src/commonMain/.../PracticeRoutineGenerator.kt) that lands once and fixes both platforms
#607 and #608 remain grouped together as the iOS parity group
The shared-module group is ordered before or independent of the platform-specific group, not merged into it

evals.prompt: Batch the open issues in milestone 9.9.9 into PRs.
evals.expected_output: A statement that no open issues carry that milestone (milestones are rarely set in this repo), and no groups — must not fall back to the whole tracker.
expectations: Response states that the milestone matched no open issues
Response contains no groups
Response does not fall back to grouping all open issues

evals.prompt: I want to launch concurrent sessions on the open P0 issues rather than review a plan — give me the waves.
evals.expected_output: Bare paste-able wave lines containing only issue numbers, with every group in a wave touching files no other group in that wave touches.
expectations: Response contains 'Wave N:' lines with comma-separated issue numbers
No issue number appears in more than one wave
Groups sharing a file never appear in the same wave
The wave lines contain no prose or commands mixed in
